must_fix.what: find_names promises that each name is found exactly once, and otherwise a ValueError says which in words. It counts distinct titles, not records, and it records a sheet's id only when exactly one record matches. So two sheets with the same title are accepted without a word. When that sheet is the one a row is found in, the call crashes with a bare KeyError.

summary: The patch does what was asked. Nothing of the owner's After Hours 07 workspace is left in the shipped tree outside the old release notes: a reverse check of the backup, read in memory, found no ids, hashes, titles or readings. All 16 affected modules pass in both looks, with the same counts the builder reported. Two things need fixing before merge. First, the run_case lines that make P01a..d work on the owner's backup (finding the names, then saying the readings back in the scene's names) are untested: removing both leaves every test green, and the cases have never run on the backup. Second, find_names breaks its 'exactly once, in words' promise: two sheets with one title pass silently, or crash with a bare KeyError when a row is found in that sheet. Smaller points: A01's 'admitted source' check could become a check of a value against itself without any test noticing; CAMPAIGN.md says too much while the release notes still quote the owner's data; found() does not page intake.items, stops on any unreadable calculation, and its reads are not logged.
